messages:
maria_g: Heads up — support ticket #CUST-4726: cust-x reports p95 API latency ~2.2s (baseline ~400ms) for requests routed to eu-west. Customer started seeing errors + timeouts after 09:10 UTC. Saw spike in our AppMetrics dashboard.

jamie_ops: I see the same in SLO view — p95 for eu-west api.gateway.request_latency jumped at 09:08 and stayed high. Any recent deploys to eu-edge? :thinking:

maria_g: no deploys flagged in the window. rolling back nothing. Opening thread to correlate routing/path.

alex_k: running quick probes from our probe cluster in eu-west1 to the customer frontend host. sharing traceroute + curl:

alex_k: ```
$ traceroute -n api.cust-x.example
traceroute to api.cust-x.example (203.0.113.22), 30 hops max
 1  10.0.1.1  0.6 ms
 2  100.64.0.5  1.1 ms
 3  198.51.100.2  12.8 ms
 4  198.51.110.9  52.3 ms
 5  203.0.113.22  250.9 ms
```

alex_k: curl timing (3 warm runs):

alex_k: ```
$ curl -w "time_namelookup:%{time_namelookup} time_connect:%{time_connect} time_appconnect:%{time_appconnect} time_starttransfer:%{time_starttransfer} time_total:%{time_total}\n" -o /dev/null -s https://api.cust-x.example/health
time_namelookup:0.002 time_connect:0.010 time_appconnect:0.650 time_starttransfer:0.900 time_total:1.120
```

alex_k: appconnect ~650ms is the kicker — TLS handshake latency inflated compared to baseline (~50-80ms). Also traceroute shows a last hop jump to a distant POP (250ms).

sre-bot: automated-note: high-p95-detection detected for channel=eng-sre metric=api.gateway.request_latency region=eu-west threshold=1.0s start=2024-10-09T09:08:00Z

jamie_ops: dns multipath? maybe our anycast announced prefix got steered to a distant peer for a subset of prefixes. Can we dig +trace from the edge node (edge-proxy-12) and from an affected customer IP? Also check if DNS returned multiple A records and one was a remote POP.

maria_g: ran `dig +short api.cust-x.example @8.8.8.8` — got two A records: 198.51.100.22 (local) and 203.0.113.22 (remote). TTL low 60s. Customer resolver might pick remote path.

alex_k: pulled flow logs from edge-proxy-12 for 09:05-09:20. Found ~12% of connections to api.cust-x.example were sent to the remote POP next-hop via our transit peer B. Looks like B started prepending an AS path that prefers one of the remote PoPs (we saw AS prepend event in bgp-monitor at 09:02).

jamie_ops: good catch. Can we confirm TLS session reuse? If connections hit remote POP, they can't reuse existing KV cache or warm tls session and we pay full handshake cost. Check `sni_metrics.tls_resumption` by backend target.

alex_k: sni_metrics shows resumption rate dropped from 78% to 12% for that SNI on the affected window.

maria_g: implications: DNS returned multipath, BGP steering caused subset of clients to a far PoP, TLS resumption lost -> p95 regression. We should mitigate: 1) reduce TTL to force fast client-side re-resolve? TTL already low. 2) Apply routing policy to prefer local anycast origination for the prefix (prefer-local in route-controller) 3) Add temporary edge-proxy sticky routing for that customer SNI to prefer local edges. Which is faster?

jamie_ops: prefer-local route-controller flip is fastest, then edge sticky. I'll open a small canary change to route-controller to bump preference for prefixes matching cust-x to 100 for eu-west, roll 1% -> 10% -> 100%.

oncall-lucy: paging in case we need BGP emergency community. I've DM'd infra-bgp-team. Also notify sales/solutions to let the customer know we're actively fixing.

alex_k: applying canary now. command used:

alex_k: ```
$ rdctl route set-preference --prefix 198.51.100.0/24 --region eu-west --preference 100 --canary 10
Applied canary to 1 edge-proxy. monitoring p95.
```

sre-bot: automation: canary applied id=rc-99872 canary=10% target=eu-west prefix=198.51.100.0/24

jamie_ops: initial canary p95 dropped from 2.2s to 520ms for traffic hitting canary proxies. Nice. increasing to 50%.

alex_k: rolled to 50%.

sre-bot: automation: canary updated id=rc-99872 canary=50%

maria_g: after 50% roll, overall p95 from customer dropped to ~580ms. Good. Please proceed to 100% and then follow up with BGPNET to root cause the peer steering.

jamie_ops: rolled to 100% at 09:41 UTC.

sre-bot: automation: canary updated id=rc-99872 canary=100% -- status=ok

oncall-lucy: customer notified (email + phone) at 09:45 UTC. Sales confirms cust-x will monitor. BGPNET says transit peer B made an accidental prepending change during maintenance; they reverted at 09:30 but some caches still persisted. We'll follow up with them for firm RCA.

maria_g: cleanup: set route preference back to default after BGPNET confirms stable, add permanent route-policy rule for SNI->local-pref for cust-x to avoid future multipath issues while bgp convergence happens, and add alert to detect sudden drop in tls_resumption per-sni.

jamie_ops: PR for alert and policy created: https://git.internal/redwood/infra/PR-1427

oncall-lucy: closing thread but leaving notes: incident-notes: cause=BGP-prepend-on-peer mitigation=route-controller-preference rollback_time=2024-10-09T10:20:00Z followups=[BGPNET-RCA, permanent-route-policy, per-sni-tls-resumption-alert]

maria_g: thanks team :heart: Customer confirmed latency back to normal range and no errors in last 30m.

alex_k: leaving trace sample and commands used in case we need to dig later:

alex_k: ```
# from edge-proxy-12
dig +short api.cust-x.example @127.0.0.1
mtr -6 -c 40 api.cust-x.example
tcpdump -n -i eth0 host 203.0.113.22 and port 443 -w /tmp/custx-handshake.pcap
```

oncall-lucy: marking resolved. will open follow-up ticket for BGPNET RCA and policy change.

maria_g: great work everyone. :thumbsup:"
